en: Verses of Praise for the Seven Buddhas (Saptabuddhastotra-gāthā).
Transmitted by the Great Master of the Teaching and Tripitaka Master, the Purple-Robed Śramaṇa and Subject Fata, from Nālandā Monastery in Magadha, Central India.
Translated by Imperial Decree: Praise to Vipaśyin Buddha. Jina-garuḍa-vikrama-rāja-prabhāsa-kīrti-pratāpa-parākrama-nirdeśa-śrī-vajra-dharmaghoṣa.
Namaḥ prakaśigarbhāya dhyānābhimukhāya | Namaḥ susthitasaṃśriye jina-viśvabhū-vaiśravaṇapramardine narakagatipraśamane jayāya || 1-4 ||

*Sāgaropamavāk-saṃkhyeya-nayana-koṭī-buddha-stuta-sarvajña-rāja-pratimā-vimala-śubha-kīrti-vardhana* (Sanskrit reconstruction). In Chinese: 娑引誐嚧伽弭嚩引誐引鄧三句倪野二合反禰泥曳反曩尾曩曳曩拶四句俱留孫佛讚野薩拽二合反弩鼻音重呼囉始銘二合短呼鉢囉二合底丁以反昧哩野二合戍引鼻一句囉㘄去引訖哩二合哆引婆去引底丁以反𭌯武。 (Translation):

"O you who are praised by Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the ocean, whose speech is like the ocean, beyond calculation, immeasurable, and infinite; O King of the All-Knowing, whose fame is stainless and pure, increasing like the light of the sun. (Note:

This is a transliteration of a Sanskrit hymn of praise (*stotra*) addressed to a Buddha, likely from a Mahāyāna sūtra such as the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-uttama-sūtra* or similar texts. The reconstructed Sanskrit provided above reflects the phonetic transcription of the Chinese characters.)

The four-line verses of Śākyamuni Buddha’s praise for this first chapter have already been circulated throughout China since the past seven Buddhas completed their own praises. May Maitreya, the future one, next extol them;
through the boundless merit of what I have composed, may all sentient beings attain liberation.
The Brahma Praise of the Seven Buddhas, one fascicle.
